source_roots: client/src server/src shared qa db docs .github
build_manifest: none — npm workspaces build every file under each workspace's src/
unit_test_scope: The changed workspaces only — `npm test --workspace=minicrm-server` if server files changed, `--workspace=minicrm-client` if client files changed. Not the whole suite: measured at 153s server and 133s client on an idle machine, far worse when oversubscribed, and the three workspaces must run in series. The full `npm run unit_test` is the Definition of Done's step, run per commit; this step is the pre-push delta.
post_fix_verification_scope: The TIA-selected set for the fix, unioned with the specs that failed — not the full suite. `server/src/scripts/select-tests.ts` resolves the diff to affected specs against `coverage_test_links`, so re-running that set is a real verdict on the new tree rather than a shortcut. Bounds are not negotiable and are in `.claude/gates/pre-push-mechanics.md` under "After the hook's own E2E run fails": the sole delta from the failed run is the fix, HEAD is otherwise unchanged, the cheap gates still run, and there is no second bypass for the same failure.
release_build_command: none — there is no production-configuration build distinct from the test build
results_file: <workspace>/test-results/junit.xml for unit tests; qa/e2e/test-results/results.xml for E2E
results_read_command: Read the XML directly. Never the console, never the exit code.
ci_results_artifact: The failing job's uploaded artifacts via `gh run view --log-failed` or `gh api`. For a healed-locator E2E failure pull that run's `healing-report.json` — the local `heal-trends.json` is from a different run and will mislead you.
verification_tiers: unit (a named test) · e2e (a functional spec, tagged) — both automated. There is no out-of-band tier: everything this project ships can be verified by something that runs here.
